prompt: Vitamin E (α-tocopherol) protects cell membranes from lipid peroxidation. By what mechanism?

options.label: Donates its phenolic O-H to ROO• (lipid peroxyl radical), giving a stable, non-propagating tocopheroxyl radical
Consumes molecular O₂ before it can react with the lipid, blocking the initiation step
Chelates Fe/Cu ions that would otherwise catalyze Fenton-type production of lipid radicals
Allosterically activates glutathione peroxidase, which enzymatically reduces lipid peroxides

explanation: Electron-rich phenols are excellent H• donors. Tocopherol's O-H gives H• to ROO•, quenching the chain. The resulting tocopheroxyl radical is heavily resonance-stabilized across the aromatic ring and is too unreactive to abstract H from a new lipid → chain-breaking. Metal chelation (vitamin C does this partly) and enzyme activation are different mechanisms.
